minutes.headline: Committee adopted three goals, raised extended day fees, and approved the coach's handbook; no FY23 budget figures yet.
minutes.summary: The committee heard the business manager explain the district's grants and clarify a figure raised at the Finance Committee. It approved routine items, three committee goals (professional development, an equity audit, media outreach), extended day rate increases and the coach's handbook. Transportation options and a possible all-rider model were previewed for a January decision.

what_happened.line: The committee approved three goals of its own: professional development, an equity audit and media outreach; the superintendent is to begin the audit action.
It approved extended day and early learning rate increases, including a new registration deposit, and approved the coach's handbook.
A transportation update previewed options, including a possible all-rider model; a survey showed strong interest in busing, and final approval is needed by January 5th.
The business manager was asked to work with the town accountant on whether the committee should report on departmental revolving funds, with the bylaw adjusted if needed.
The committee accepted the FY22 quarterly budget update; several negative balances are being resolved and no deficits are anticipated.

why_it_matters: Families with children in extended day or early learning programs will pay higher rates, and a busing fee or all-rider model could add a new charge for families that now ride free.
Revolving funds are spending outside the main school appropriation, so any annual reporting the committee adopts would show residents money that does not appear in the general budget line.
